sentences.text: Exams can sometimes make us feel nervous, especially if they are in a language we are still learning.
But don't worry.
In this episode, I'm going to teach you how to speak English confidently and answer questions clearly.
You will learn how to introduce yourself to the examiner.
Common phrases used in English exams.
How to ask for help or clarification if you don't understand a question.
How to manage your time and stay calm during the exam.
How to answer different types of questions in an exam.
Polite speaking tips and how to use body language.
How to stay confident and calm even if you're nervous.
How to make a good impression on the examiner.
Introducing yourself in the exam.
When you start the exam, the examiner may ask you to introduce yourself.
This is very common and it's your chance to feel a bit more relaxed and comfortable before the exam begins.
Common phrases to introduce yourself.
Hello, my name is Emily.
I am from your country.
I am here for my English exam.
I live in city country.
I am very excited to be here today.
Nice to meet you.
Example dialogue.
Hello, my name is Emili.
I am from Turkey.
Nice to meet you, Emily.
Are you ready for your exam?
Yes, I'm a little nervous but I am ready.
Tip, stay calm, smile and speak clearly.
The examiner will appreciate it if you are polite and confident.
Common phrases used in English exams.
During an English exam, you may hear different types of questions and it's important to know how to answer them.
Let's look at some useful phrases and strategies.
If the examiner asks you to describe something, this is a picture of a beach.
There are three people in the picture.
The weather looks sunny and warm.
I think the person is smiling.
Can you describe the picture?
Yes, of course.
In the picture, there is a family at the beach.
The mother is wearing a hat and the father is holding a towel.
There is a child playing with a ball.
The sky is clear and the water is blue.
If you don't understand the question, sometimes the examiner may ask a question that you don't understand.
It's important to ask for clarification so you don't make a mistake.
Sorry, can you repeat the question, please?
I didn't understand.
Could you speak more slowly?
Sorry, I'm not sure what you mean.
Can you explain again?
Example dialogue.
What is your opinion about the importance of learning English?
Sorry, could you repeat the question, please?
I didn't understand.
Sure, I said, what is your opinion about the importance of learning English?
Oh, I think learning English is important because it helps you communicate with people from many countries.
It also helps with finding good jobs.
Tip.
If you don't understand, always ask for clarification.
Don't be afraid to ask.
Managing your time and staying calm.
Exams can be stressful, but managing your time and staying calm are key to success.
Here are some helpful tips.
Time management tips.
Listen carefully to the instructions.
Don't spend too much time on one question.
If you don't know the answer right away, move on to the next question.
You can come back later.
Take deep breaths and give yourself time to think.
It's better to give a thoughtful answer than to rush and make a mistake.
Staying calm.
If you feel nervous, take a moment to breathe.
Smile and remember that the examiner is there to help you.
Don't worry about small mistakes.
It's okay to make mistakes during the exam.
The important thing is to try your best.
Example dialogue.
What do you like to do in your free time?
Hmm.
Let me think.
I like reading books and watching movies.
In the summer, I enjoy going to the beach with my friends.
I also like traveling and visiting new places.
Tip.
If you feel nervous, focus on breathing slowly and speaking clearly.
Don't rush.
Answering different types of questions in an exam.
In an English exam, you will be asked different types of questions.
Let's practice how to answer them.
One personal question.
These questions are about you, your life and your opinions.
They are usually the easiest to answer.
What is your name?
My name is Emily.
Where are you from?
I am from Turkey.
What do you like to do in your free time?
I like reading books, cooking and listening to music.
Example dialogue.
What do you like to do in your free time?
I like reading books and watching movies.
I also enjoy traveling with my family.
Tip.
Describing a picture.
You may be shown a picture and the examiner will ask you to describe it.
Here are some helpful phrases.
In this picture, I see there are many people in the picture.
The weather is sunny and everyone looks happy.
Example dialogue.
Can you describe this picture?
Sure.
In the picture, there is a park.
There are trees and flowers.
People are walking and sitting on benches.
The weather is sunny and everyone looks happy, giving your opinion.
Sometimes the examiner will ask for your opinion on a topic.
You can use these phrases to answer.
In my opinion, I think that I believe that.
Example dialogue.
What do you think about studying in a foreign country?
In my opinion, studying in a foreign country is a great experience.
You can learn new things, meet new people and improve your language skills.
Tip.
Be honest and use simple, clear sentences.
Don't worry about making mistakes.
Polite speaking and body language tips.
Being polite and using good body language during the exam can leave a positive impression on the examiner.
Polite phrases to use.
Excuse me, can you repeat the question?
Thank you for your question.
I'm sorry, I don't know the answer, but I will try my best.
Good body language tips.
Sit up straight and look confident.
Make eye contact with the examiner.
Smile to show you are friendly and confident.
Use hand gestures if necessary, but keep it natural.
Examiner, what is your favorite holiday?
My favorite holiday is Christmas.
It's a time to spend with family and give gifts.
It's a very special time for me.
Tip.
Make eye contact.
Speak clearly and use positive body language.
Final tips for your English exam.
Practice speaking before the exam.
Listen to English podcasts and practice answering questions.
Don't worry about mistakes, it's okay to make them.
Be confident, polite and stay calm.
Take deep breaths if you feel nervous.
Closing.
I hope this episode has helped you feel more prepared for your English exam.
Remember, stay calm, speak clearly and don't be afraid to ask for help.
Thank you so much for listening.
If you enjoyed this episode, please subscribe to my podcast and share it with your friends.
Good luck on your exams.
See you next time.
Bye -bye.
